entities.name: Artemis Fowl
entities.label: Text
entities.summary:
Artemis Fowl is a fantasy adventure novel series by Irish author Eoin Colfer, comprising eight books published between 2001 and 2012. The series centers on Artemis Fowl II, a twelve-year-old Irish criminal mastermind who discovers that a civilization of fairies (the 'People') exists below the Earth's surface, and his increasingly complex interactions with LEPrecon (Lower Elements Police Reconnaissance) fairy officer Holly Short.

The series combines the conventions of the crime thriller, science fiction, and fairy tale genres in a contemporary urban fantasy setting. Artemis Fowl himself is a deliberately ambiguous protagonist — presented initially as a villain who kidnaps Holly Short for ransom — who gradually evolves into an anti-hero and eventual hero as the series progresses. Colfer's world-building is notable for its systematic integration of Irish fairy mythology (the Tuatha Dé Danann tradition) with science fiction technology, creating a hidden civilization beneath human society with plasma cannons, time-stop technology, and biometric scanners.

The series was a major commercial success, selling over 25 million copies worldwide. It was compared to Harry Potter and launched alongside the first wave of early-2000s fantasy series. A Disney film adaptation was released in 2020 (directed by Kenneth Branagh) to poor critical reception. The series is significant for introducing younger readers to themes of moral ambiguity, environmental ethics (fairy civilization threatened by human pollution), and intelligence as heroism — with a protagonist defined by his mind rather than conventional heroic virtues.
